title: Chicken breast, grilled without sauce, skin not eaten

content.title: About
content.content: Chicken breast is a lean cut of meat taken from the pectoral muscle of the bird. Grilled without sauce and without the skin, it retains a natural flavor and tender texture while being low in calories.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chicken breast contains less fat than other parts of the bird such as thighs or wings.
Grilling helps preserve more nutrients compared with deep‑frying.
It is one of the most affordable sources of complete protein.
Proper grilling creates a small amount of aromatic compounds that give a characteristic smoky taste.
Chicken breast is a staple in many diet plans and athletic nutrition programs.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: A 100 g serving provides about 31 g of high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Skinless grilled breast contains less than 3 g of fat per 100 g, making it suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: It is high in niacin (B3) and vitamin B6, which support energy metabolism and nervous‑system function.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Provides phosphorus, selenium and zinc, important for bone health, immune function and antioxidant protection.

items.title: Low glycemic impact
items.content: Does not cause a rapid rise in blood glucose, beneficial for people monitoring blood sugar.

items.title: Food‑borne illness risk
items.content: Undercooked chicken may harbor Salmonella; ensure internal temperature reaches 75 °C.

items.title: Bird meat allergy
items.content: A small number of individuals may be allergic to chicken proteins.

items.title: Sodium content in marinades
items.content: If the breast is pre‑marinated, sodium levels can be high; choose low‑salt options.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Slice the grilled breast for salads, wraps, soups, or use it as a protein base for bowls. It pairs well with vegetables, whole grains, and light sauces such as yogurt or lemon‑based dressings.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep raw breast in the refrigerator at 0–4 °C for up to 2 days. Cooked breast can be stored in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 3 days or frozen for up to 2 months.
